method: Repository-first. Publisher Version of Record or complete publisher HTML was inspected only where existing repository evidence was not enough to freeze source-native central operators. No preliminary MAIN structural outcomes were inspected.

sources.adopted_edition: Springer Nature Version of Record, published 2024-02-29, complete publisher HTML
sources.raw_sha256_unavailable_reason: PR #438 baseline contains no publisher PDF/HTML raw-byte acquisition for ATT-01; the official complete publisher VoR HTML is source-readable but raw transport bytes were not available to this lane.
source_loci: Algorithmic Model: integrated priority map Eq.3
bounded_native_findings: Feature-specific saliency, learned selection-history, task weights and previous-trial feature-dimension effects are combined into an integrated priority map followed by softmax-like priority selection.
Priority is mapped to ex-Gaussian response-time parameters; seven source-defined model variants/ablations are compared.
The source-native target is behavioral selection-history integration, not a divisive visual-cortical normalization network.
direct_ancestry_notes: Existing ATT audit found no direct citation to Makwana ATT-B1; non-citation is explicitly not treated as independence evidence.
No DOI-qualified direct model ancestor is asserted by W1.
adverse_limits: No raw publisher byte hash is frozen in the PR #438 baseline.
Complete correction-registry nonexistence is not claimed.
Whole model-family ancestry remains non-exhaustive.

sources.adopted_edition: PLOS Computational Biology publisher Version of Record PDF/complete HTML, published 2016-02-18
source_loci: bottom/top layer divisive normalization Eqs.2-3 and Eqs.5-6
bounded_native_findings: Two reciprocally connected visual layers use local untuned divisive inhibition; top-down attention is applied to the higher layer and redistributed to the lower layer by modulatory feedback.
The model explicitly cites Reynolds & Heeger 2009 (ATT-03) as a detailed normalization model, while arguing for a distinct higher-area feedback architecture.
The model is instantaneous and omits fine temporal dynamics, synchrony/noise-correlation effects and surround suppression.
direct_ancestry_notes: ATT-03 is a direct theory comparison/citation and shared normalization constituent; W1 does not assert that ATT-02 is a direct mathematical descendant of the full ATT-03 model.
adverse_limits: S1 parameter sensitivity shows +20% changes can eliminate many modeled effects.
Top-down source is deliberately unspecified.
No exhaustive correction-registry proof.

sources.adopted_edition: PLOS Computational Biology publisher Version of Record PDF/complete HTML, published 2019-04-09
source_loci: Methods Eqs.2-4 flat posterior and leaky counts
S1 File Supplementary Results referenced by main article
bounded_native_findings: The hierarchical learner tracks two transition probabilities plus a shared global change-point variable, allowing confidence about an unobserved transition to reset when the other transition signals a coupled change.
The flat comparator uses leaky beta-count inference and can approximate first-order probability estimates but lacks coupled confidence transfer.
The paper directly cites Glaze et al. 2015 (BLF-03) when discussing leaky integration and prior adaptive-learning work; citation alone is not a direct-descendant proof.
direct_ancestry_notes: Glaze 2015 is an explicit source citation but is used as background/comparator evidence; no direct derivation of the BLF-02 hierarchical coupled-transition model from BLF-03 is asserted.

correction_or_supplement_bundle.note: PLOS S1 File; main text explicitly points to Supplementary Results for flat-model/delta-rule equivalence and heuristic controls. Raw supplement bytes are not frozen in PR #438 baseline.

adverse_limits: Task structure is instructed rather than discovered by the model.
Correct task structure is only moderately identifiable from one subject's observations.
Flat and hierarchical first-order estimates can be highly correlated; confidence is the stronger discriminator.
S1 File raw hash remains unavailable in the PR #438 baseline.

sources.adopted_edition: eLife Version of Record, published 2015-09-28; repository receipt targets publisher v2 PDF
source_loci: Version history distinguishing Accepted Manuscript 2015-08-31 from Version of Record 2015-09-28
Fig.1-2 hazard-dependent leak and stabilizing boundary
bounded_native_findings: Belief is updated in log posterior odds by adding current LLR to a hazard-dependent nonlinear prior transform of the previous belief.

Expected instability produces adaptive leak near uncertain beliefs and a hazard-dependent non-absorbing stabilizing bound at stronger beliefs; H=0 gives perfect integration and H=0.5 discards history.
Discrete- and continuous-time formulations are source-defined; suboptimal leaky-only and bounded-only approximations are compared.
direct_ancestry_notes: The article derives its rule from Bayesian switching-state inference and cites earlier dynamic-learning and sequential-sampling work; W1 does not promote generic Bayesian/HMM background to a unique direct model ancestor.
adverse_limits: Human subjects learn hazard rates imperfectly, overestimating low rates and underestimating high rates.
Suboptimal approximations capture some regimes but not the full data.
Accepted-manuscript and Version-of-Record dates are distinct and must not be silently conflated.

sources.adopted_edition: Nature Human Behaviour Version of Record, published online 2023-10-16, complete open-access publisher HTML
sources.raw_sha256_unavailable_reason: PR #438 baseline records a 15-page publisher PDF opened in-browser but no frozen raw publisher PDF/HTML SHA256. W1 uses the exact open-access Version-of-Record HTML for bounded semantic qualification without inventing a byte hash.
bounded_native_findings: A dynamic latent concept library is coupled to an adaptor grammar; favored programs and subparts are cached and reused as primitives in later composition.
Inference samples programs/libraries with Pitman-Yor/Gibbs machinery and applies explicit resource bounds to composition/search.
AGR mixes forward and backward phase predictions; rational-rules and subsymbolic comparators are separate model variants.
direct_ancestry_notes: The source explicitly says it adapts Liang, Jordan & Klein (ICML 2010), 'Learning programs: a hierarchical Bayesian approach'.
The source reference has no DOI; W1 therefore does not fabricate a DOI-valued direct_model_ancestor entry.
adverse_limits: Deterministic likelihood cannot efficiently represent vague concepts.
No conditional primitive is included, so some divide-and-conquer reports are inexpressible.
Raw publisher byte hash remains unavailable in the PR #438 baseline.
Exact DOI-qualified identity of the explicitly adapted Liang 2010 ancestor is unavailable in the source bibliography.

sources.adopted_edition: PLOS Computational Biology publisher Version of Record PDF/complete HTML, published 2024-04-25
source_loci: Model architectures: RNN, logistic regression, MLP
bounded_native_findings: The study trains recurrent neural networks for transitive inference and systematically varies which feedforward/recurrent weights are trainable and the regularization/initial-connectivity constraint regime.
Feedforward logistic-regression and single-hidden-layer MLP comparators test whether recurrence/working-memory dynamics are required.
Multiple trained RNN solutions generalize with distinct behavioral and population-dynamics predictions; network training is not claimed as a literal brain learning algorithm.
direct_ancestry_notes: Prior task-trained RNN and transitive-inference literature is cited, but W1 found no source statement of direct descent from CNC-03/C-HORSE or another selected MAIN model.
adverse_limits: Some RNNs fit all training trials yet fail to generalize.
Several qualitatively different RNN solutions remain viable; further neural data are required to distinguish them.
The paper explicitly does not interpret RNN optimization as the brain's task-learning mechanism.

sources.adopted_edition: eLife Version of Record, published 2023-12-11; repository receipt targets publisher v1 PDF
source_loci: autoencoder training across three category tasks
bounded_native_findings: C-HORSE maps EC input/output through DG, CA3 and CA1 with two complementary pathways: a sparse highly plastic trisynaptic pathway and a more distributed slower-learning monosynaptic pathway.
TSP specializes in exemplar-specific rapid binding/pattern separation; MSP learns category regularities and generalizes to novel exemplars.
The model is trained as an autoencoder and evaluated on three category-learning paradigms; pathway lesions isolate complementary contributions.
direct_ancestry_notes: The source states that this C-HORSE variant was developed for statistical learning in Schapiro et al. 2017b and Zhou et al. 2023.
Schapiro et al. 2017b is DOI 10.1098/rstb.2016.0049 and is adopted as a DOI-supported direct model ancestor.

The broader lineage explicitly includes Ketz et al. 2013, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003067, plus earlier Norman/O'Reilly models; this is recorded as shared lineage rather than all being promoted to immediate direct ancestors.
adverse_limits: The model isolates hippocampal contributions and omits interactions with basal ganglia, prefrontal cortex and other cortex.
The model architecture is inherited C-HORSE lineage rather than an independent-from-scratch network family.
Version of Record must not be conflated with peer-review/revision artifacts.
